hints: Focus on what excess acidified K2Cr2O7 does to each functional group, and count how much [O] each change needs.
Remember that a primary alcohol needs 2[O], while a secondary alcohol needs 1[O] and an aldehyde needs 1[O] for complete oxidation.
Look for the structure where the [O] demands add up to exactly 3 and where oxidation of an alcohol explains the H2O product.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidation rules with excess oxidant**

With excess acidified K2Cr2O7, primary alcohols go fully to carboxylic acids, secondary alcohols go to ketones, and aldehydes go to carboxylic acids.

$$\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + 2[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{R}_2\text{CHOH} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{CO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{RCHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}$$

**Use the equation to count oxygen atoms**

The equation is $\text{X} + 3[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{Y} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, so X must consume exactly 3[O] in total and must contain an alcohol to make the $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
This rules out structures that need too much [O] or make no water.

**Test structure A**

Structure A is $\text{OHC-CH(CH(OH)CH}_3\text{)-CHO}$. It has two aldehydes and one secondary alcohol.
Demand is $1 + 1 + 1 = 3[\text{O}]$, exactly matching the equation, and the secondary alcohol oxidation gives the $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with a single organic product Y.

options.A: Contains two -CHO groups (1[O] each to become -COOH) plus one secondary -CH(OH)- group (1[O] to become ketone plus H2O). Total is 3[O] and one H2O is formed, giving one dicarboxylic keto-acid Y. This fits X + 3[O] -> Y + H2O perfectly.
options.B: This is a triol with three primary -CH2OH groups. Each primary alcohol needs 2[O] to reach -COOH, so full oxidation would need 6[O], not 3[O]. It cannot fit the given equation.
options.C: This is glycerol, HOCH2-CH(OH)-CH2OH, with two primary alcohols and one secondary alcohol. Full oxidation needs 2 + 2 + 1 = 5[O], not 3[O], so it does not match.
options.D: This is a trialdehyde, OHC-CH(CHO)-CHO. Each aldehyde needs 1[O], so total is 3[O], but aldehyde oxidation makes no H2O. The equation would be X + 3[O] -> Y with no water, so D is a tempting trap.
